title: Engagement Manager (HCM Implementation, People Manager)
jobDescription:
About Darwinbox

Darwinboxis Asia's fastest-growing HR technology platform, designing the future of work by building the world's best HR tech, driven by a fierce focus on employee experience and customer success, and continuous, iterative innovation. We are the preferred choice of 1000+ global enterprises to manage their 4 million+ employees across 130+ countries. Darwinbox's new-age HCM suite competes with local as well as global players in the enterprise technology space (such as SAP, Oracle, and Workday). The firm has acquired notable customers ranging from large conglomerates to unicorn start-ups: Nivea, Starbucks, DLF, JSW, Adani Group, Crisil, CRED, Vedanta, Mahindra, Glenmark, Gokongwei Group, Mitra Adiperkasa, EFS Facilities Management, VNG Corporation, and many more. Our vision of building a world-class product company from Asia is backed by marquee global investors like Microsoft, Salesforce, Sequoia Capital, TCV, KKR, and Partners Group.


What this role is

Darwinbox is transforming how enterprises manage people, workflows, and employee experiences at scale. As we evolve, implementation is no longer about configuration and delivery tracking. The real challenge is helping organizations rethink how HR should operate across systems, processes, adoption, and decision-making.

This role sits at the intersection of:

  • Enterprise consulting

  • Product thinking

  • Customer transformation

  • Large-scale Saa S delivery

You will act as:

  • A trusted advisor to enterprise customers

  • A strategic partner to CHROs and business leaders

  • The “Voice of Customer” internally across Product and Engineering

  • An owner responsible for customer outcomes — not just go-live milestones

What the work looks like

  • You won’t just inherit a project plan. You’ll inherit ambiguity.

  • A customer struggling to standardize processes globally.

  • An implementation that technically works, but operationally doesn’t.

  • A workflow designed for manual operations that now needs to scale intelligently.

Your role is to understand the business problem behind the requirement and drive the transformation end-to-end.

That means:

  • Leading enterprise HCM transformation programs from discovery through adoption

  • Challenging legacy processes and driving transformation conversations

  • Influencing senior stakeholders with clarity and credibility

  • Working closely with internal teams to shape customer outcomes

  • Balancing customer expectations, scalability, product capabilities, and operational realities

Because enterprise transformation breaks when those worlds operate separately.

Who thrives here

  • People who think in systems.

  • People who naturally ask: “Will this scale?” / “What breaks after go-live?” / “Are we solving the actual customer problem?”

  • People with consulting instincts, strong ownership mindset, and executive presence.

  • People who care equally about customer outcomes, product experience, and operational excellence.

What we explicitly don’t optimize for

  • Coordination-heavy implementation profiles

  • Delivery managers who only track timelines

  • Requirement takers who never challenge assumptions

  • Governance without ownership

  • Implementation thinking without business context

What we’re looking for

  • 6–12 years of experience in enterprise Saa S, HCM implementation, consulting, or transformation roles

  • Strong stakeholder management and executive communication skills

  • Consulting mindset with ability to drive transformation conversations

  • Strong customer advocacy and product-oriented thinking

  • Data-driven and automation-first approach to problem solving

Lastly, what we are not looking for , we’re not looking for traditional implementation managers nor project coordinators and definitely not people who measure success by whether the tracker is green.

title: Project Manager
jobDescription:
About Darwinbox:

Darwinbox is Asia's fastest-growing HR technology platform, designing the future of work by building the world's best HR tech, driven by a fierce focus on employee experience and customer success, and continuous, iterative innovation. We are the preferred choice of 900+ global enterprises to manage their 2.5 million+ employees across 116+ countries.

Role Overview

As Project Manager within Delivery, you will own governance and operating rigor across the Darwinbox implementation lifecycle—from sales handover, kick-off, execution, go-live, hypercare, and transition to Customer Success. You will ensure standardized Inflexion process adherence, proactive risk management, delivery excellence, portfolio visibility, and leadership reporting.


Key RESPONSIBILITIES:

1. Project Governance & Delivery Excellence

• Own implementation governance, process adherence, documentation, approvals, customer sign-offs, and stage-gate compliance before each phase progresses.

• Provide a holistic project view across functional implementation, integrations, payroll, dependencies, risks, delivery milestones, and stakeholder requirements.

Manage client and internal stakeholders requirement and drive successful engagement.


2. Implementation Lifecycle Management

• Manage pre-kick-off readiness including contract/SOW reviews, sales handover, Account Playbook, high-level plan, partner PODs, Share Point setup, and PM tool onboarding.

• Drive kick-off readiness from technical checklist completion to end-to-end delivery plan preparation.

• Run client kick-offs, scrums, plan updates, RAID logs, PM tool tracking, Mo Ms, production migration, hypercare readiness, Customer Success handover, closure reporting, and NPS trigger.


3. Project Health, Risk & Governance Reporting

• Monitor project health, flag Amber/Red trends early, escalate risks, delays, and planning gaps, and drive timely mitigation with Implementation and Delivery leaders.

• Conduct governance cadence including Steer Cos, WSRs, portfolio reviews, governance decks, and leadership updates covering progress, hours, escalations, actions, owners, and timelines.


4. Knowledge Management, CS Transition & Portfolio Operations

• Document customer interactions and decisions through Mo Ms, BBPs, and structured Share Point folders, ensuring knowledge transfer before closure.

• Govern Implementation-to-Customer Success transition by tracking stage gates, context, open risks, ownership transfer, and closure readiness.

• Build dashboards and reporting frameworks for capacity, utilization, billable/productivity, gross margins, R/A/G health, delivery risks, and customer lifecycle status.

• Act as the operational bridge between Implementation and Customer Success, ensuring smooth handovers and a complete operational picture.


Minimum Requirements

• 8–12 years of Program / Project Management experience leading large-scale enterprise product implementations or programs.

• 6+ years of cross-functional team management experience, preferably in a Saa S / enterprise product company.

• Strong understanding of Saa S business models, implementation lifecycles, Agile methodologies, and tools such as Rocketlane, JIRA, or Atlassian

• Strong analytical, problem-solving, organizational, executive communication, presentation, and stakeholder-management skills.

• Ability to grasp technical subjects and relevant technologies; bachelor’s degree or equivalent work experience.


Preferred Requirements

• Ability to switch between tactical execution and strategic responsibilities while managing multiple priorities efficiently.

• Experience building delivery-operations dashboards and governing implementation-to-Customer Success transitions in enterprise Saa S.


Why Join Us

Join Darwinbox to help transform enterprise HR technology while bringing governance, predictability, and proactive risk management to every customer journey.

title: AI-Native Systems Builder
jobDescription:
AI-Native Systems Builder

We're looking for builders.

Not product managers. Not software engineers. Not AI researchers. People who happen to do all three when the problem demands it — because they care more about solving the problem than about which lane it falls in.

What this role is

Darwinbox is an enterprise HCM platform used by hundreds of large organizations across multiple countries. We're in the middle of a fundamental shift — rearchitecting the product and the company to be AI-native. Not adding AI features to an existing system. Rebuilding how the system thinks, operates, and delivers value.

This role exists because the most important work in that transformation doesn't fit traditional job boundaries. It sits at the intersection of product thinking, systems engineering, enterprise domain knowledge, and AI — and it requires people who can hold all of that in their head while shipping something that actually works.

You will take ambiguous, high-stakes enterprise problems and turn them into working systems. Some will be customer-facing product capabilities. Some will be internal operational systems. All of them will require you to think deeply about the realities of enterprise software — permissions, auditability, multi-tenancy, scale, configurability, edge cases — because that's where most "AI-powered" systems quietly break.

What the work looks like

You won't get a detailed spec. You'll get a problem.

It might sound like: "Our customers can't tell whether their employees are actually using the platform — and neither can we." Or: "Implementation consultants spend 40% of their time on work that should be systematized." Or: "This workflow was designed for humans filling forms — redesign it for a world where AI handles 80% of the steps."

Your job is to go from that problem statement to a production system. You'll need to understand the business context, design the solution, build it (using AI-native development workflows extensively), validate it against real enterprise complexity, and iterate until it works — not in a demo, but at scale, with real customers, in production.

Who thrives here

People who build things outside of work — not because someone asked, but because they saw a problem and couldn't leave it unsolved.

People who use AI tools daily and have strong opinions about where they're transformative and where they're dangerous.

People who think in systems — who instinctively ask "what breaks downstream?" and "what happens at 100x scale?" and "what's the edge case no one mentioned?"

People who've shipped things. Not prototyped. Shipped. In environments where the user didn't forgive rough edges.

You might come from engineering, product, consulting, design, operations, or a path that doesn't have a clean label. We genuinely don't care about the label. We care about how you think, how you simplify, and what you've built.

What we explicitly don't optimize for

  • Resume pedigree as a proxy for capability
  • Interview performance on problems you'd never encounter here
  • AI enthusiasm without AI execution
  • Coordination-heavy profiles that produce slides instead of systems
  • Prototype thinking without production realism

Why this role exists

Most companies hire PMs to write specs, engineers to execute them, and analysts to measure the outcome. Three roles, three handoffs, three points of context loss.

We're building a company where one person can hold the full arc — problem to system to outcome — because we believe that's how the best enterprise software gets built in the AI era.

If that sounds like how you already think, we should talk.
